# **📑 HUMAN IK (HIK) GUIDE		13th Sept 2022**				

“HIK can be considered a very versatile rig once you know how to handle it\!”

						\~ Anonymous Lemon

### **🧷 BETTER SAFE THAN SORRY…**

Now that you will be using HIK, just as a precaution, please make the following changes in your Maya preference.

![][image1]

### 

### 

### **👋 WELL, HELLO THERE HIK…**

When you open/reference a HIK rig into the scene, the very first thing you will need to do is click that little human icon at the top right corner of the screen which will add a tab called Human IK.

![][image2]

Clicking the Human IK tab will open up the default picker, however, it might come out looking a little buggy like the bottom left image (if it doesn’t, that’s good). To solve this, just click on another tab, and then return to the Human IK tab, you should be getting something like the bottom right image which means all is good\!

![][image3]![][image4]

Now that the HIK picker is up and running, there are 6 areas that you would frequently touch on…

![][image5]

#### **⚪ WHITE  **  

Normally used for baking to the skeleton or the control rig. 

![][image6]![][image7]

* Do note that there is a difference in “Bake Control Rig” and “Bake Rig Body Part”	  
* “Bake Control Rig” means it’s a complete full bake of all the controls from the picker (this excludes hidden controls). You will get this option if you are under the ***FULL*** or ***INDIVIDUAL*** body selection only  
* “Bake Rig Body Part” means that it will bake only the selected body part of your individual selection. Eg. you are selecting the L wrist and applying the Bake Rig Body Part, it will bake the entire L arm only. You will get this option if you are under the ***HALF*** body selection

  #### **🟢 GREEN** 

* Used for changing character pickers and also for re-targetting other HIK motions(sourcing & copying other motions)

  #### **🔴 RED** 

* Used to alternate between 3 types of body selections  
* From left to right, they are ***FULL***, ***HALF*** and ***INDIVIDUAL*** body selections  
* ***FULL*** 	selection means that if you move or key a single part of the body, everything will follow and be keyed  
* ***HALF*** 	selection means that if you move or key a single part of the body, 	only the selected body area will follow and be keyed  
* ***INDIVIDUAL*** body selection means that if you move or key a single part of the 	body, only that specific part that is being selected will move or be keyed only  
* Under ***INDIVIDUAL*** body selection, only joints and IK effectors (green) can be moved around

  #### **🟡 YELLOW** 

* Used for pinning the translation and rotation of an effector  
* From left to right, they are the translation pin and rotation pin  
* The pin selections will work best when it is under the ***HALF*** and ***FULL*** body 	selection, it is advisable to avoid using it in ***INDIVIDUAL*** selection

#### **🟣 PURPLE** 

* The default picker for all HIK  
* Can be separated to effectors and bone 	  
* Effectors can be identified by the circle-looking controls whereas bones are identified by the straight-looking controls. 	

  ![][image8]![][image9]

* Effectors have both translate and rotation attributes whereas joints/bones only have rotation

  ![][image10]![][image11]


* Do note that the spine bone selection actually has 3 controls packed into 1 selection. You can find each spine control from the outliner and the graph editor

  ![][image12]


* **❗❗ Be careful as there are 4 	hidden controls not present in the picker. They are the Head , L\&R Toe and the elusive Hips bone which can only be found in the outliner. Take note that there are no effectors or joints being selected from the picker in the image below ❗❗**

  **![][image13]**![][image14]

  ![][image15]

  **Normally, in motions that have the 1st and last pose the same, you would wanna pay attention to these hidden controls**

* If you are selecting an effector, you can also create a pivot effector 	or an aux effector by **right clicking on it**. The maximum number of pivot/aux effectors that can appear on a selected effector are 4 only, any more than that and it will appear in the outliner

  ![][image16]![][image17]


* For pivot effectors, press D and you should be able to move it to the location of your choice, press D once more when you are done again to lock it in place	  
* **For aux effectors, you can think of them as locators that have become the master control of the original control** 	 	  
* If you 	would want to select the entire body, just click on the empty area 	around the HIK. However, by doing so, it does not mean that the fingers or the toes are being selected…you will need to manually go into the fingers and click on the empty areas for them to be selected

  ![][image18]![][image19]

  #### **🔵 BLUE** 

* Normally you will be touching the IK Blend T (translation) and R (rotation) only, which is actually the same as the Reach Translation and Reach Rotation attribute

  ![][image20]

* Setting the value as 1 makes the effector green which means its an IK and 0 makes it turn grey which makes it FK 	  
* You do not necessarily need to have both translation and rotation the same colour at the same time

  ![][image21]

* When an effector is set as FK (grey) and is under the ***INDIVIDUAL*** 	selection, you will not be able to move it around…however, if it was under ***HALF*** or ***FULL*** selection, then, it is possible to move it around  
* At the 	moment, you can ignore the IK Pull


  ### **🔄 RE-TARGETTING FROM ONE CHARACTER TO ANOTHER CHARACTER…**

* Bring in the HIK rig of your choice (the pink man in this case) and a 	reference existing pose/motion which can be of any HIK rig  
  	![][image22]

**Character1 is referring to the pink man**

* Under Source, change it from Control Rig to the reference pose/motion that you have brought in

  ![][image23]

* You will notice Character1 immediately snapping to where the existing 	reference pose/motion that you brought in

  ![][image24]

* Bake your animation to the Control Rig and Euler filter it

  ![][image25]

* Remove the 	reference and you should have the same animation as the reference itself\! 	  
  	![][image26]

### **🔁 RE-TARGETTING FROM AN FBX TO ANOTHER CHARACTER…**

* **Before proceeding, this method of retargetting will also depend on the name 	of the bones/joints. This means that if the fbx data uses a different bone/joint naming compared to the HIK rig that you would like to use, then IT WILL NOT WORK. Take the image below as an example…**

  **![][image27]**

  **Both the pelvis have a different name, the pink character’s pelvis is called“Bip001\_Pelvis” whereas the fbx data’s pelvis is called “pelvis”**


  If the name of both pelvis and other relevant bones are the same, then you may proceed…

* Relatively similar as how you do it from one character to another, the only 	difference is that you are dealing with one character and an fbx file which contains the data from a mocap session 	  
* Bring in the HIK rig of your choice and set the Source from Control Rig to None

  ![][image28]

* Drag and drop the fbx into the scene and you should see the character 	performing the fbx motion  
* Bake to the Control Rig and Euler filter, you are done\!
